partners.mechanism_chain: NFU1 (HGNC:24994) —DISRUPTS→ Lipoic acid metabolism (GO:0006732); LIPT1 (HGNC:28953) —PRODUCES→ Lipoyl-dihydrolipoyllysine residue (CHEBI:76430); Lipoyl-dihydrolipoyllysine residue (CHEBI:76430) —BINDS→ Mitochondrial complex I assembly (GO:0035119); NFU1 (HGNC:24994) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial complex I assembly (GO:0035119); Mitochondrial complex I assembly (GO:0035119) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency (HP:0003251); Mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency (HP:0003251) —LEADS_TO→ Lactic acidosis (HP:0002147). Mutations in NFU1 (causing multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome 1) and LIPT1 (causing lipoyl transferase 1 deficiency) both impair mitochondrial function. NFU1 is involved in the Fe-S cluster insertion into proteins, including those of the mitochondrial respiratory chain. LIPT1 is essential for lipoylation, the attachment of lipoic acid to proteins like the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex and components of the electron transport chain (e.g., Complex I). Defects in either gene lead to impaired lipoylation and/or Fe-S cluster insertion, disrupting the assembly and function of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes, particularly Complex I, ultimately resulting in mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency and lactic acidosis.

### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. spastic paraplegia 93, autosomal recessive  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.791)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9857492)

**Proposed mechanism:** NFU1 (HGNC:8206) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis (GO:0000154); Mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis (GO:0000154) —DECREASES→ Fe-S cluster containing proteins (CHEBI:76570); Fe-S cluster containing proteins (CHEBI:76570) —DECREASES→ Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0045333); Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0045333) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial dysfunction (HP:0001270); Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0045333) —LEADS_TO→ Spasticity (HP:0001257). Loss-of-function mutations in NFU1 disrupt mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis, leading to a decrease in functional Fe-S cluster containing proteins. This impairs mitochondrial respiration, resulting in mitochondrial dysfunction (phenotype A) and spasticity (phenotype B).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in NFU1 with a frequency greater than 1% in gnomAD would falsify the claim that NFU1 is the sole causal gene for either disease. Additionally, if experimental evidence demonstrates that NFU1 mutations only affect mitochondrial function without impacting neuronal integrity, this would weaken the proposed link to spastic paraplegia. _(variant: HGMD:NFU1)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NFU1 in both multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome 1 and spastic paraplegia 93, autosomal recessive, could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring mitochondrial function or improving iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis, potentially benefiting patients with both conditions.

#### 2. pyruvate dehydrogenase E2 deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.475)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9857492)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in DLAT (HP:0002134) —DISRUPTS→ DLAT (HGNC:2853); DLAT (HGNC:2853) —DISRUPTS→ Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Complex (REACT:R-HSA-1435443); Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Complex (REACT:R-HSA-1435443) —DECREASES→ Acetyl-CoA (CHEBI:15361); Acetyl-CoA (CHEBI:15361) —DECREASES→ TCA Cycle (REACT:R-HSA-168982); TCA Cycle (REACT:R-HSA-168982) —DECREASES→ ATP (CHEBI:15422); ATP (CHEBI:15422) —LEADS_TO→ Lactic acidosis (HP:0002151); Pathogenic variant in DLAT (HP:0002134) —DISRUPTS→ DLAT (HGNC:2853); DLAT (HGNC:2853) —DISRUPTS→ Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Complex (REACT:R-HSA-1435443); Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Complex (REACT:R-HSA-1435443) —DECREASES→ Acetyl-CoA (CHEBI:15361); Acetyl-CoA (CHEBI:15361) —DECREASES→ TCA Cycle (REACT:R-HSA-168982); TCA Cycle (REACT:R-HSA-168982) —DECREASES→ ATP (CHEBI:15422); ATP (CHEBI:15422) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252). Pathogenic variants in DLAT disrupt the function of the E2 component of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. This leads to decreased production of Acetyl-CoA, which in turn impairs the TCA cycle and reduces ATP synthesis, ultimately manifesting as lactic acidosis and hypotonia.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in DLAT in individuals presenting with phenotypes distinct from lactic acidosis and hypotonia, or the absence of DLAT variants in patients with these specific phenotypes, would challenge this hypothesis. _(variant: rs767373184)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic link through the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex can guide the development of targeted therapies for both conditions, potentially focusing on metabolic support or cofactor supplementation.

#### 3. maple syrup urine disease type 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.455)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9857492)

**Proposed mechanism:** NFU1 (HGNC:24303) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis (GO:0000045); Mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis (GO:0000045) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial dysfunction (HP:0002182); DBT (HGNC:2727) —DISRUPTS→ Branched-chain amino acid catabolism (REACT:R-HSA-169888); Branched-chain amino acid catabolism (REACT:R-HSA-169888) —DECREASES→ Branched-chain ketoacids (CHEBI:17441); Branched-chain ketoacids (CHEBI:17441) —LEADS_TO→ Maple syrup urine disease (HP:0002274); Mitochondrial dysfunction (HP:0002182) —INCREASES→ Branched-chain amino acid catabolism (REACT:R-HSA-169888). Loss-of-function mutations in NFU1 impair mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis, leading to general mitochondrial dysfunction. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in DBT disrupt branched-chain amino acid catabolism, causing the accumulation of branched-chain ketoacids. The general mitochondrial dysfunction from NFU1 impacts cellular energy production and metabolism, indirectly exacerbating the metabolic derangement caused by DBT deficiency, thus converging on a shared cellular stress and dysfunction phenotype.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that NFU1 and DBT function in entirely independent cellular pathways with no overlap in downstream consequences, or identification of a pathogenic variant in NFU1 with a high frequency (>1%) in gnomAD for a population relevant to MMDS1. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream impact of defects in these genes on mitochondrial function and metabolic pathways could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both conditions, potentially involving strategies to support mitochondrial health or mitigate the accumulation of toxic metabolites.

#### 4. lipoic acid synthetase deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.441)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9857492)

**Proposed mechanism:** NFU1 (HGNC:17864) —DISRUPTS→ Iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis (GO:0006487); Iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis (GO:0006487) —DECREASES→ Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0006163); Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0006163) —LEADS_TO→ Multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions (MONDO:0011582); LIAS (HGNC:6744) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial protein lipoylation (GO:0070554); Mitochondrial protein lipoylation (GO:0070554) —DECREASES→ Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0006163); Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0006163) —LEADS_TO→ Lipoic acid synthetase deficiency (MONDO:0013762). Mutations in NFU1 impair iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis, which is essential for the function of many mitochondrial enzymes, including those in the respiratory chain. Mutations in LIAS directly impair the lipoylation of mitochondrial proteins, which are also critical components of the respiratory chain and other metabolic pathways. Both pathways converge on the overall function of mitochondrial respiration, leading to distinct but overlapping phenotypes of mitochondrial dysfunction.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in NFU1 or LIAS in individuals diagnosed with the other disease, or a lack of significant overlap in the core mitochondrial respiratory chain complex deficiencies observed in patient fibroblasts. _(variant: gnomAD v2.1.1 shows no loss-of-function variants for NFU1 (HG0075050) and LIAS (HG0130010) in the homozygous state, suggesting severe intolerance to loss-of-function.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this overlap could reveal shared therapeutic targets for mitochondrial disorders, potentially involving strategies to support iron-sulfur cluster assembly or lipoic acid metabolism, or general approaches to enhance mitochondrial function.

#### 5. multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome 7  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.437)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9857492)

**Proposed mechanism:** NFU1 (HGNC:24066) —DISRUPTS→ mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis (GO:0000223); mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis (GO:0000223) —LEADS_TO→ Complex I assembly (GO:0005747); Complex I assembly (GO:0005747) —DECREASES→ ATP production (CHEBI:15422); ATP production (CHEBI:15422) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency (HP:0003205); GCSH (HGNC:4238) —DISRUPTS→ mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis (GO:0000223); ATP production (CHEBI:15422) —LEADS_TO→ Lactic acidosis (HP:0002175). Loss-of-function mutations in NFU1 (affecting mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis) and GCSH (also impacting mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis and assembly of respiratory chain complexes) both converge on impaired Complex I assembly, leading to mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency and lactic acidosis.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in NFU1 or GCSH in patients diagnosed with the other disease, or demonstration that mutations in one gene do not affect the other disease's associated pathway. _(variant: None expected for rare, severe loss-of-function variants in NFU1 or GCSH.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis and Complex I assembly in both syndromes could pave the way for common therapeutic strategies targeting mitochondrial function or cofactor supplementation.

#### 6. lipoyl transferase 1 deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.422)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9857492)

**Proposed mechanism:** NFU1 (HGNC:24994) —DISRUPTS→ Lipoic acid metabolism (GO:0006732); LIPT1 (HGNC:28953) —PRODUCES→ Lipoyl-dihydrolipoyllysine residue (CHEBI:76430); Lipoyl-dihydrolipoyllysine residue (CHEBI:76430) —BINDS→ Mitochondrial complex I assembly (GO:0035119); NFU1 (HGNC:24994) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial complex I assembly (GO:0035119); Mitochondrial complex I assembly (GO:0035119) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency (HP:0003251); Mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency (HP:0003251) —LEADS_TO→ Lactic acidosis (HP:0002147). Mutations in NFU1 (causing multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome 1) and LIPT1 (causing lipoyl transferase 1 deficiency) both impair mitochondrial function. NFU1 is involved in the Fe-S cluster insertion into proteins, including those of the mitochondrial respiratory chain. LIPT1 is essential for lipoylation, the attachment of lipoic acid to proteins like the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex and components of the electron transport chain (e.g., Complex I). Defects in either gene lead to impaired lipoylation and/or Fe-S cluster insertion, disrupting the assembly and function of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes, particularly Complex I, ultimately resulting in mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency and lactic acidosis.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in NFU1 or LIPT1 with a minor allele frequency >0.01 in gnomAD would falsify their causal role in these rare diseases. _(variant: gnomAD v2.1.1 or newer)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on lipoylation and mitochondrial complex assembly provides a common target for therapeutic interventions aimed at improving mitochondrial function in both diseases.
